title: Migrating off CPQ at functional parity
deck_lead: Salesforce has set an end-of-sale date on Salesforce CPQ. This document sets out one scoped path off it: what it covers, what it leaves out, and what it costs. Client-specific slides are marked and filled during the pursuit.
_note: Illustrative example for the skill. Not a live client quote.

slides.left_lead: A supported process running on an unsupported platform.
left: Quoting, pricing, and approvals run through CPQ.

slides.title: Why this approach fits
slides.pick_note: Functional parity migration over twelve weeks. Scope is confirmed from the Analyze inventory and re-baselined before Design if the source org exceeds the basis of estimate.

reasons.head: The inventory does not justify remediation
reasons.body: Discovery points to a small custom-code footprint. Reconstructing that logic into the rules engine is a service we offer and this engagement is not expected to need it.

reasons.head: Parity is the stated goal
reasons.body: The client asked for the same process on a supported platform. A redesign extends the timeline past the deadline that created the project.

reasons.head: The deadline binds the schedule
reasons.body: Twelve weeks clears end of sale with margin. The heavier options run seventeen and twenty four weeks.

slides.title: Scope boundaries
in_scope: Product catalog migrated one to one, with hierarchy, attributes, and rules.
Pricing procedures, discount schedules, and decision tables.
Quoting, the transaction line editor, and approvals up to three chains.
Order creation and activation from accepted quotes.
One documented integration, re-pointed and re-tested.
Data migration for product, pricing, and contract records.

out_scope.item: Pre-migration cleanup of the source org
A second org, a split, or a merge
Integrations beyond the one in the approach
